name: UK energy price cap
summary: The typical dual-fuel energy price cap is set to rise 26% to about £2,166 a year from 1 January on higher gas prices
state: Cornwall Insight forecast on 18 Nov that the typical dual-fuel cap will rise 26%, or £443, to £2,166 a year for 1 Jan to 31 Mar 2027, up from the current £1,723 (City AM; ITV News). The rise is attributed to higher international gas prices linked to the Middle East conflict. A rise of 26% exceeds the 20% Alert line, although the cap level itself stays below £2,200. Searches on 28 Nov found no change to that picture.
for_you: Households on standard variable tariffs face higher bills from 1 January, with the largest effect on those in poorly insulated homes or on low incomes. Ofgem's website explains how the cap works and where to find help with bills.
rubric_hit: Forecast cap rise 26% ≥ 20% Alert line (cap £2,166, below £2,200 level line)

sources.title: ITV News — Winter energy bill misery on way as price cap set to jump by 26% in January
City AM — Households set for £443 increase on energy bills

why: The Ofgem cap sets bills for most UK households — a direct cost-of-living signal.
drivers: Wholesale gas and power prices, network costs, policy levies.

rubric.normal: Typical dual-fuel cap < £1,700/yr and next forecast change < +5%.
